name: Ghanshyam option-buying course (2022): hammer / star, 2:20 candle, Fibonacci 0.71, breakouts
source: Ghanshyam option-buying course transcript (72 pages, recorded 2022), shared by Mandeep 11 Nov 2026
about: Rules from the course, written with the app's facts (2.68 gun pieces: open_fall / open_rise, hs_conf, am_move, pm_rng / pm_edge, fib_dday / fall_day, fib_uday / rise_day, and the pm / fib38 / sig stops). Thresholds are the course's rules scaled to today's prices (his 100-150 Bank Nifty points at ~42,000 = about 0.3%); the example-day numbers in the course (42,000, premium 300 to 350, 28-point candles) are illustrations, not targets. The 9:20 strategy is in the earlier file ghanshyam_920. Checked before this file on Bank Nifty 2022-2026 (index 1-minute data and the 5-year Lab's real option prices, all charges): his favourite hammer did NOT hold up (31-33% win, negative in both halves); the shooting star after a rise on a gap-down day was the best candle lead (small sample); the 2:20 break WITH the morning move lost money in every period (an 'avoid' check), AGAINST it and away from the middle of the range was the best lead (+Rs 150 / -730 / +370 per trade train / validation / holdout, not proven); Fibonacci 0.71 after a fall worked only after a big fall (0.8%+), mixed. Every strategy here starts on trial (test bench only); nothing goes live or in the alerts until it passes the Lab on data it never saw and you switch it on. v2 (12 Nov 2026, Mandeep: can 2 lots make 5% / 10%?): every setup also has option-premium targets of +6% and +11% (about +5% / +10% of the money after charges for a Rs 30K lot), with the course's own stops.

strategies.name: Shooting star after a rise, gap-down day (full size)
strategies.note: Course V1: trading below yesterday's close, a rise of 100-150 points from the open, a shooting star at the day's high; buy puts when a close breaks its low (within 3 bars); stop above the star; book when a candle closes above the previous one. Claim '8 of 10': not supported (51% win, n 35 on 2022-2026), but the best candle lead.

strategies.name: Shooting star after a rise, above yesterday's close (half size)
strategies.note: Course V1: the same star after price climbed back above yesterday's close: he trades half size (lower accuracy).

strategies.name: Hammer after a fall, gap-up day (full size)
strategies.note: Course V1: trading above yesterday's close, a fall of 100-150 points from the open, a hammer at the day's low; buy calls when a close breaks its high; stop below the hammer. Claim '90% over 100 trades': not supported (31-33% win, negative 2022-24 and 2025-26). Kept on trial so the Lab records it.

strategies.note: Course V1: the hammer after price fell below yesterday's close: half size.

strategies.name: Hammer at yesterday's close (support)
strategies.note: Course V2: a hammer at yesterday's close (support) 'works very well'. Within 0.15% of yesterday's close.

strategies.name: Shooting star at yesterday's close (resistance)
strategies.note: Course V2 mirror: a shooting star at yesterday's close (resistance).

strategies.name: 2:20 candle break against the morning move, call (not mid-range)
strategies.note: Course V3: break of the 14:15-14:20 candle's high, stop at its low, out on a close below the previous candle or by ~15:00; not when the candle sits in the middle of the afternoon range; a break against the earlier trend moves better. Best 2:20 lead in the check (+Rs 150 / -730 / +370 per trade), not proven.

strategies.name: 2:20 candle break against the morning move, put (not mid-range)
strategies.note: Course V3 mirror: break of the 2:20 candle's low after a rising morning.

strategies.name: AVOID check: 2:20 break with the morning move, call
strategies.note: Control: the same break in the direction of the morning move lost money in every period (-Rs 250 to -630 per trade). Expected to fail; kept to confirm the 'avoid' check on new data.

strategies.name: AVOID check: 2:20 break with the morning move, put
Fibonacci 0.71 call after a fall from the day's high
strategies.note: Course V5: after a strong fall, buy calls when price crosses back above the 0.71 retracement; stop at 0.38; target 1 = back at the high (about 0.9R), target 2 = the 1.27 extension (about 1.7R). Calls only in the course. All falls of 0.5%+: negative in the check.

strategies.name: Fibonacci 0.71 call after a big fall (0.8%+)
strategies.note: Course V5: 'only after a good downfall with strength (700 points, not a 300-point drift)'. Mixed lead in the check (swing stop 2R: +Rs 373 / +734 / -339).

strategies.name: Fibonacci 0.71 put after a big rise (mirror, never tested in the course)
strategies.note: He uses Fibonacci for calls only and says he never tested puts: this mirror is our own trial.

strategies.name: Breakout after a pause, with the daily trend (call)
strategies.note: Course V4: trade breakouts after price pauses at the level (5-20 minutes), full size with the trend. His '7 of 10 with a pause' was not supported in the check (the 'ideal' breakout was no better than others).
